paper_a.title: A local lemma via entropy compression

paper_b.title: Entropy Compression Method and Legitimate Colorings in Projective Planes

metadata.description: Both papers use the entropy-compression / Moser-Tardos record-injection technique. Paper A (Alves-Procacci-Sanchis) develops a general entropy-compression theorem (EC-Lemma) covering arbitrary tidy-flaw settings and applies it to several graph-coloring problems. Paper B (Bissacot-Doin) instantiates an Esperet-Parreau-style entropy-compression bound (with an added register entry gamma to handle non-elementary bad settings) to prove a new upper bound on legitimate d-colorings of finite projective planes. The hypothesised relation SM (same method) is well supported: both papers carry the same scaffolding (variable setting, register/record vector, lossless reconstruction lemma, partial-Dyck/tree-sum or phi_E generating function bound) and differ in scope (general theorem with multiple coloring corollaries vs. one concrete projective-plane application).

matches.explanation: Both define the variable-version Moser-Tardos setting: a finite collection of mutually independent discrete random variables and a family of bad events depending on subsets of variables. Both cite Moser-Tardos and (in 418) Kolipaka-Szegedy. Same object, same role.

Paper A's EC-setting (atoms/colors/objects/flaws) plus the exponent set E_O and degree multiplicities d_j play the same role as paper B's bad-setting indexing data (mathcal{Z}, C_i, k_i, m_i, l_i, E, d_l): both bundle the combinatorial data needed to feed the entropy-compression bound. Paper A factors out the seed/power machinery (DP414.5) whereas paper B keeps k_i and m_i in flat form, so the framing differs but the data are the same.

Paper A introduces 'power' kappa_y / ||e_y|| of an event via seeds (effective size), which is what enables non-elementary tidy flaws. Paper B does not use this notion explicitly; in its setup the size l_i is just |Z_i| - k_i with k_i fixed companions playing a similar role but without the seed-minimality machinery. Paper-original to A.

Tidy flaw / seed: paper A's central definition that licences non-elementary flaws in the variable setting. Paper B does not introduce a seed/tidy concept; its variant of Esperet-Parreau handles non-elementary bad settings by storing the configuration label gamma in the register instead. Paper-original to A.

The register vector R = (alpha, beta, gamma) of paper B is its specific encoding of the run-trace; paper A uses a different encoding (the record string R_t in PSP414.1 with entries r_i = 0 or (j, ell)). The two encodings play the same role but the gamma component is the headline novelty of paper B (Remark RP418.1) and has no direct analog in paper A's record. Listed paper-original to B; the conceptual match to paper A's record sits at the proof-step level (PSP414.1) and is captured below in the proof alignment.

Both are iterative random-coloring algorithms in the Moser-Tardos / Esperet-Parreau family: at each step pick the smallest-index uncolored variable, sample a value from a fresh entry of an input vector, and on a bad-setting / flaw resample-or-uncolor. Paper A's EC-Algorithm uncolors obj(e) minus the seed G(e,y); paper B's variant resets the l_y non-companion variables. Same algorithm template, slightly different bookkeeping. The composite many-to-many step alignment ASP414.1-4 vs ASP418.1-5 is captured here implicitly: initialize - main loop - branch on bad setting - update / return correspond pairwise (init ~ ASP418.1, main loop ~ ASP418.2, branch ~ ASP418.3, termination/return ~ ASP418.5; paper B factors register update into its own step ASP418.4 which paper A folds into its branch step).

Both are entropy-compression existence-and-running-time theorems. Paper A's EC-Lemma states: if k > inf_x phi_O(x)/x then a good coloring exists and the algorithm finds it in expected time linear in |S|. Paper B's Theorem 1 (a variant of Esperet-Parreau) states: there exists a coloring avoiding bad settings using ceil(gamma sup_i (d_{l_i} m_i)^{1/l_i}) colors, where gamma = phi_E'(tau) and phi_E(tau) - tau phi_E'(tau) = 0. The two bounds are the same Drmota / generating-function constant phi'(xi) = min phi(x)/x (= gamma in paper B) applied to the same generating function family; phi_O of paper A and phi_E of paper B coincide when the d_l multiplicities are encoded the same way. Confidence high because the mathematics agrees up to notation, but flagged 'analogous' rather than 'exact' because paper A's tidy-flaw + power(seed) generality strictly extends paper B's setting (and conversely paper B carries the m_i factor explicitly to handle non-elementary configurations).

The full proof of paper A's EC-Lemma (TP414.4) - record map M, partial-Dyck-words bound, tree-sum via Drmota - is paper-A material with no full counterpart in paper B (paper B cites Esperet-Parreau / Theorem 1 as a tool rather than reproving its analytic-combinatorics core). Paper B does, however, reproduce the lossless-compression piece (its Lemma 2 = LP418.2) which corresponds to paper A's Lemma 3.2 (LP414.2); that match is recorded separately.

Both lemmas state that the set of uncolored variables/atoms after step i is a deterministic function of the recorded register/record vector alone. Paper A's X_t = gamma_t^{-1}(0) determined by R_t; paper B's X_i determined by (R_j)_{j<=i}. Same statement, same proof technique (induction on i).

Both are the injectivity / lossless-reconstruction lemma at the heart of entropy compression: paper A's M : F_t -> (R_t, gamma_t) is injective; paper B's ((R_j)_{j<=i}, phi_i) determines all colors used. Both proofs are induction on i with case split on whether the register entry at step i is empty or encodes a bad setting (compare PP414.3/PSP414.4-6 with PP418.1/PSP418.1-4).

Same induction-on-i proof of the injectivity / reconstruction lemma. The proof-step structure matches: paper A's PSP414.4 (base) corresponds to paper B's PSP418.1; PSP414.5 (case r_t=0) corresponds to PSP418.3 (R_i empty); PSP414.6 (case r_t = (j, ell)) corresponds to PSP418.4 (R_i = (alpha, beta, gamma)). The composite step-level alignment is captured by this single parent-level entry per the v2 prompt rules.

Paper A's separate induction proof of LP414.1 (X_t determined by R_t) has no separate proof in paper B - paper B states the analogous LP418.1 without an extracted proof node, so the structural counterpart is implicit only.

The Lovasz Local Lemma (TP414.1) and Cluster Expansion Local Lemma (TP414.2) are cited external scaffolding in paper A (it explicitly compares its EC-criterion to CELL throughout). Paper B does not invoke LLL or CELL directly; its comparison is to Esperet-Parreau (TP418.2). Paper-A external context that has no paper-B counterpart in the JSON; emitted as 'none' here only because TP414.1/2 are the headline results being compared in paper A's Section 1, but per the compactness rule for external nodes this is the boundary case - tagged high confidence 'none' since paper B simply does not engage these particular results.

Both are the cited prior-art entropy-compression / algorithmic-LLL theorem that the paper's main theorem extends. Paper A cites Moser-Tardos + Pegden's algorithmic CELL; paper B cites Esperet-Parreau (which is itself a generalization of Moser-Tardos for forbidden configurations). The two cited results sit in the same lineage (Moser-Tardos -> Pegden / Esperet-Parreau) but are distinct theorems, hence 'analogous' rather than 'exact'.

Moser-Tardos algorithm cited as external in paper A. Paper B's algorithm AP418.1 is itself a Moser-Tardos / Esperet-Parreau variant (already aligned with paper A's EC-Algorithm AP414.2 above), so MT is implicit ancestry rather than a separately extracted node in paper B. External-origin scaffolding.

Natural dependency graph (Moser-Tardos) is external scaffolding cited by paper A. Paper B does not extract this definition - its setting goes straight from independent variables to bad events without an explicit dependency-graph definition node. External-origin in paper A.
Symmetric LLL criterion ep(d+1) <= 1 cited from Erdos-Lovasz; paper B does not reference the symmetric LLL criterion. External-origin in paper A.
Clique estimate of Xi_e is paper A's Section 1.3 device for comparing its EC-criterion to CELL; paper B does not perform this comparison.
Strong variable-setting CE criterion (rewritten) is paper A's Section 4.1 reformulation for the comparison theorem PrP414.3; no counterpart in paper B.

Partial Dyck words and D_{n,r,E} are paper A's combinatorial counting machinery (Section 3.1). Paper B inherits the analogous bound implicitly via citing Esperet-Parreau / Theorem 1 (TP418.1), but does not unfold the Dyck-word / tree-sum combinatorics into its own definition node.

Lemmas 3.3-3.6 of paper A (partial-Dyck / tree-Dyck bijection / record-to-Dyck map / pre-image bound) are the analytic-combinatorics core of paper A's main proof. Paper B does not reproduce these - it consumes them packaged inside Theorem 1. Paper-A original.

Paper A's Propositions 3.1 (cardinality bound for failure set) and 3.2 (tree-sum bound for |R^r_t|) are the technical backbone of its proof. Paper B does not state or use analogous propositions - it black-boxes them via Theorem 1. Paper-A original.
Drmota's tree-sum asymptotic is external scaffolding for paper A's EC-Lemma proof. Paper B does not cite Drmota. External-origin in paper A.

Paper A's Proposition 4.1 (EC criterion dominates strong CE criterion) compares EC against CELL in the variable setting. Paper B does not perform this comparison; its Esperet-Parreau-vs-EC remark space is different.

Both papers apply their entropy-compression theorem to specific coloring problems. Paper A gives six worked examples (non-repetitive vertex coloring, star coloring, beta-frugal coloring, acyclic vertex coloring, acyclic edge coloring, independent transversals). Paper B's parallel application is the legitimate-coloring problem for projective planes (ProbP418.1) with the resulting bound packaged in the Proposition (PrP418.3). The match is at the role level: 'apply the EC theorem to a specific graph-coloring problem and read off the bound.' The actual problems differ. Listed many-to-many because in both papers these are the suite of concrete payoffs of the abstract method. Per v2 compactness, examples normally do not need 'none' entries; this composite is included because the analogy is the SM (same-method) signal itself.

Per v2 compactness rules, remark nodes do not need 'none' entries. Including this composite only to flag that both papers carry several methodological remarks but the remarks address different topics: paper A's RPs are about CELL-vs-LLL improvement and the acyclic-edge-coloring lineage; paper B's RPs are about the new gamma register entry, uniform-case limitation and an optimization restatement. Low confidence because the remarks are heterogeneous.

Paper B's Definition 'Bad setting' = pair (Z, c) of a vertex subset and a coloring of it that should be avoided. Paper A's analogous primitive is the 'flaw' inside DP414.3, but DP414.3 is a much richer composite (atoms, colors, objects, flaws together); the bare bad-setting pair is paper-B framing without a separate counterpart in paper A. Counted paper-original to B.
Dangerous pair (two distinct lines whose type vectors are within 22 ln n in l1) is specific to the projective-plane application of paper B. No counterpart in paper A. Paper-original to B.

Optimal block size m-bar minimizing the entropy-compression bound for projective-plane colorings. Paper-B-specific optimization variable; paper A's analog would be the optimizing x in inf_x phi_O(x)/x but the m-bar block-size parametrization is paper-B specific. Paper-original to B.
The constant K and the bounds P_a, P_b on dangerous-pair probabilities are paper-B equations specific to the projective-plane probabilistic argument (Facts 1 and 2). No counterpart in paper A.

Fact 1 (existence of small set S hitting every line of a projective plane), Corollary on |S|, and Fact 2 (partial coloring with bounded dangerous incidences) are the projective-plane probabilistic-method machinery of paper B. Paper A has no analog: its applications use the EC-criterion directly without an analogous probabilistic preprocessing step.
Proofs of paper B's Corollary on |S|, Fact 1, Fact 2, and the legitimate-coloring proposition. All projective-plane-specific; no counterpart in paper A.

Paper B's variable-version forbidden-configuration coloring problem (find a coloring of V avoiding all bad settings). The conceptual analog in paper A is the implicit 'find a coloring in the intersection of complements of all flaws' problem solved by the EC-Lemma TP414.4, but paper A does not extract a separate problem node. Listed paper-original to B.

Proofs of paper A's combinatorial-counting machinery (Proposition 3.1, Lemmas 3.3-3.6, Proposition 3.2). All belong to paper A's analytic-combinatorics core (Dyck words, tree-Dyck bijection, Drmota application). Paper B black-boxes this layer behind its citation of Theorem 1 / Esperet-Parreau.

Paper B's open problem on whether the small-vs-large-order gap for legitimate colorings of P_n is intrinsic or an artifact of entropy compression. Projective-plane-specific; no counterpart in paper A.
